notes: P&G sold the Ivorydale bar-soap plant in 2003 to Trillium Health Care Products of Brockville, Ontario, a contract manufacturer of about 200 to 300 employees, and no later sale of the soap plant turned up.
Spray Products is its own company, founded in 1958 and run by the founder's son Bart Bastian from Plymouth Meeting, Pennsylvania, so it is independent but headquartered outside Ohio.

Exsurco is a subsidiary of Bettcher Industries of Birmingham, Ohio, which MPE Partners owned from 2017 until KKR bought it in late 2021; Bettcher's own plan shows about 350 participants, and with its Georgia units Cantrell and Gainco the group may sit near 500 but no count above that was found.
No sign of a parent turned up for the Portsmouth flooring maker; its website is gone and news coverage is thin, so this rests on nothing contrary found.

Tronair is itself the operating platform, headquartered in Swanton, Ohio, and owned by private-equity firm Golden Gate Capital since 2016; its own plan shows about 350 to 400 participants and its add-on brands (Columbus Jack, Malabar, Eagle Tugs) are small, so no larger parent was found.
AMG Industries describes itself as a single-site Mount Vernon metal stamper founded in 1904 as Akron Metallic Gasket, and no parent company turned up.
PureCycle: Ohio LLC, the Ironton plant, is a subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed PureCycle Technologies of Orlando, Florida, which reported 177 employees at the end of 2022.
RevLocal was run by founder Marc Hawk with angel and minority equity backing (about 450 employees in 2020) until H.I.G.-backed Hibu bought it in August 2024, after the grant years.
KEMBA Credit Union of West Chester is a member-owned credit union, so no company owns it, and no merger during the grant year turned up.
Nullable Inc. is Columbus startup Aware, venture-backed and independent through the grant years; Mimecast bought it in August 2024, just after fiscal 2024 ended.
Wauseon Machine is owned by Cornerstone Corporation, a Dublin, Ohio holding company whose holdings are the Wauseon businesses themselves, so the parent is small and Ohio-based.
JobsOhio describes PowerBuilt as founded in 2000 by Rick Hauck and headquartered in Bellefontaine, and no parent or sale turned up.

Heidtman Steel of Toledo says it invested in Fulton County Processing in 2005 and lists the Delta plant as one of its locations; Heidtman's own plans show roughly 1,000 participants, though the size of its stake before FCP took the Heidtman name around 2023 is not stated.
Rimeco Products calls itself a family-owned CNC machine shop near Cleveland, run by the Ribic family.
Ingage Partners, a Cincinnati IT consulting firm, became owned by its employees through an ESOP in 2018 and no outside parent turned up.
Riffle Machine Works is a family-founded Chillicothe supplier to Kenworth, founded in 1980, and no parent company turned up.

VRI of Franklin, Ohio was itself the operating platform, owned by private-equity firm Pamlico Capital, through fiscal 2021; ModivCare announced its purchase in August 2021, after that fiscal year ended.
Lake Shore Cryotronics was family-owned by the Swartz founders' company through fiscal 2024; Arcline-backed DwyerOmega bought it in June 2026, well after the grant year.
